edit.description: The home: two `pub(crate) const`s beside `MARKETPLACE_FIELD` (:223), whose own doc already states this pattern's reason — "the one home the SDK's edge declaration and the reference graph that resolves it both name, so the edge field and the value it reads cannot drift apart". One names the key a matcher group carries its handler array under (`hooks`), one the single field lifted beside it (`matcher`), each carrying the SDK's cite at the point of claim (`sdk/src/builtins.ts`:506,:510 — code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, "Matcher patterns", retrieved 2026-09-29). The first in-file consumer is the legacy-lock normalization at :932-:933, which restates both literals to reconstruct the shape a lock written before the `entry_shape` column carried implicitly.

The `hook` built-in's `EntryShape::GroupArray` at :300-:301 — the declaration every other site in the tree is a copy of — names the two constants instead of its literals. The in-crate unit test at :1076-:1077 asserts the same pair: name the constant on the declaration side only and leave the assertion's expected value spelled out, since a constant on both sides of an `assert_eq!` proves nothing about the wire.

Four spellings over two concepts, neither of them install's to name. The handler-array key: `session_start_group` (:1996) builds `{hooks:[{type,command}]}`, `group_has_command` (:2020) reads it back off a group, `gate_hook_fields` (:2371,:2374) authors the matcher-plus-handlers pair a scaffolded member module carries. The outer settings key already has a home this file does not use — `CollectionKeyPath::HooksEvent.collection_key()` (`src/kind.rs`:234, "the one place the wire key paths map to their manifest object, so the adapter's walk names no literal of its own") — while `fresh_settings` (:1918), `merge_settings` (:1962,:1980,:1981) and `event_has_command` (:2010) each spell `hooks` raw. Both folds land here; the second is the one the existing home was written for.

The read/write face takes `member_key` and `lifted_fields` as parameters and names no literal of its own — already correct, and the shape the rest folds toward. Only its unit-test fixture restates the pair (:1126-:1127) to drive `manifest_members`; name the constants in that fixture and in the `hook_matcher_group` call arguments (:1156,:1174,:1190), and keep the wire-shaped `assert_eq!` expectations (:1110,:1179) literal for the same reason as the built-in's test.

Listed for the fence, expected untouched: the integration crate cannot see a `pub(crate)` constant, and its assertions read the bytes install actually wrote, so they stay literal by design (`engineering.md`, "A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote"). Widening the constant to `pub` to reach here is the wrong move — "An export earns its consumer", and the consumer is in-crate.

summary: One home for the hook group's wire keys — `hooks` and `matcher` are bare literals at six engine producer sites, while the SDK names each exactly once.

tests.asserts: the `hook` kind's collection address still pins the `hooks`/`matcher` group-array spelling, with the expectation side spelled literally
install's settings merge and its gate-hook scaffold write byte-identical output — the fold changes no behavior
the hook read/write round-trip over a real manifest stays green

acceptance: cargo test green, clippy/fmt clean, and `rg '"hooks"|"matcher"' src/` resolves to the two constants' definitions plus only the named non-identities: `src/bundle.rs`'s plugin `hooks/hooks.json` top-level key (a different manifest's schema, not this key), and the wire-pinning assertions in the two unit tests.
notes: The second half of the HOOK-AUTHORS fence capture, drained from `.flume/refactor/` this tick. Gated at the tail of the install.rs chain not for size — it is small — but because GATE-COMMANDS-GENERATE-ACROSS-THE-SEAM and INSTALL-NAMES-A-GATE-HOOKS-REMEDY both reshape `gate_hook_fields` and its neighbours; folding a literal under a caller about to move is churn. scoped at 55af999f
